page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on KVM virtualization. Its hardware relies on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via Hyper-Threading. The allocation provides a dedicated vCPU model supported by 33 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. System memory totals 64.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or integrated graphics accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and featuring a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate capabilities in memory throughput and key-value database operations alongside standard compute limitations. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths measure 39.75 GB/sec and 36.51 GB/sec respectively, while PassMark CPU tests achieve an overall score of 7037.75. Redis SET performance reaches 5.94 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core and multi-core CPU metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench register in lower performance tiers, and LLM text generation rates remain low for larger model sizes.

Given its high memory allocation relative to processing cores, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations that do not require high CPU compute density. The lack of local NVMe storage necessitates external persistent disk provisioning. Appropriate workload fits include in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, relational database buffer caches, memory-bound background tasks, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM capacity per virtual core.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 4 physical cores, 8 dedicated vCPUs, and 64.0 GB of RAM, it delivers an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio alongside 33 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector instructions. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, while local disk storage and GPU hardware are absent. Performance data shows stable memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks at 39.75 GB/sec read speed and strong Redis SET throughput reaching 5.94 million operations per second, despite lower rankings in raw CPU stress benchmarks. The resource profile makes this instance cost-effective for memory-bound workloads that require low-to-moderate processor utilization, such as in-memory caches, database caching tiers, and memory-heavy enterprise backend processing.
